method: All eight printed pages read from the supplied Part 1 PDF (2x whole-page renders plus 6x crops of table rows, numbers and captions). Every stored answer index checked against the print: all 135 pre-existing keys were correct; one printed value was wrong in the bank (DI osmolality) and fixed; questions re-sequenced to the traversal; five uncovered captions/rows/boxes given items (140 total).
caveats: p740: prints 'Imepenem + cilastatin' (standard: imipenem); taught as printed with the standard spelling in the stem.

p741: 'Sweet - Beta ketothiolase deficiency' is printed without the article; the abnormal-values table prints urine osmolality '< 200 mOsm/kg' for diabetes insipidus (the earlier bank said 300 - corrected).
p743: prints 'leucocyte' in the factors heading and 'leukocytes' in the table; both forms accepted in stems.
p746: prints 'Acute Interstitial Necrosis (AIN)' - the usual expansion is nephritis; taught as printed and flagged in MED-C7-116.
p745/p746: photograph content (cast images) is not tested beyond its printed captions.

pages.traversal: Chapter title 'URINE ANALYSIS'; 'Urine Collection' heading; Sample, Analysis, Preservation, Storage lines; 'Instructions: To Avoid' two bullets; 'Catheterised patients' two bullets; photo caption 'Collection of urine'; 'Physical Properties' / APPEARANCE table rows 1-7 top-to-bottom; jar caption 'Normal urine colour'; ODOUR table rows Pungent, Musty/mousy, Curry/maple syrup, Sweaty feet (two bullets). Timestamps/Active space excluded.

elements.source: Sample: 2nd urine sample of morning -> midstream technique.
Analysis: within 2-4 hours at room temperature (pH to be checked immediately).
Preservation: Formaldehyde, Glutaraldehyde.
Storage: 2-8 C upto 12 hours.
To avoid: strenuous physical activity 72 hrs prior -> false results due to rhabdomyolysis.
To avoid: collection during menstruation.
Catheterised patients: always collect fresh urine; do not collect from urobag.
Photo caption: Collection of urine.
APPEARANCE rows 1-2: Light yellow - Normal; Pale/white - up water intake.
Pink - Desferrioxamine, beetroot.
Darkening on long standing - Imepenem + cilastatin (printed spelling).
Green - Triamterene (ENaC blocker).
Brown - Nitrofurantoin.
Orange - Rifampicin, Entacapone (COMT inhibitor).
Appearance table consolidation (match / odd-one-out after all rows).
Photo caption: Normal urine colour.
ODOUR: Pungent - infection (unless proven otherwise) d/t ammonia produced by bacteria.
Musty/mousy - Phenylketonuria; Curry/maple syrup - MSUD; Sweaty feet - isovaleric acidemia, glutaric aciduria type II.

pages.traversal: Odour table continued: Cabbage-like / Rancid butter (one condition), Cat urine, Acid smell, Fish urine, Sulfurous, Sweet, Swimming pool; OTHER PROPERTIES table rows pH, specific gravity, osmolality (urine then blood cell); CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE / Acidification diagram (alpha-intercalated cell, H+ ATPase, H+/K+ ATPase, NH3->NH4+, HPO4->H2PO4-); Concentration three bullets; Abnormal values table rows 1-4.

elements.source: Cabbage-like; Rancid butter - Tyrosinemia type I (single merged condition).
Cat urine - multiple carboxylase deficiency (MCD).
Acid smell - methyl malonic acidemia (MMA).
Fish urine - Trimethylaminuria.
Sulfurous - Cystinuria; Sweet - Beta ketothiolase deficiency.
Swimming pool - Hawkinsinuria (table consolidation).
pH: urine 4-4.5 (acidic); blood 7.35-7.40.
Specific gravity: urine 1.020-1.040; blood 1.010.
Osmolality (mOsm/kg): urine 800-900; blood 285-290.
Acidification: alpha-intercalated cells of cortical collecting duct (CCD); luminal H+ ATPase; H+/K+ ATPase.
NH3 + H+ -> NH4+: non titratable, major acid.
HPO4 2- + H+ -> H2PO4-: titratable acid.
Concentration: ADH from posterior pituitary -> free water reabsorption; medullary interstitium up osmolality d/t urea; vasa recta.
Urine pH > 5.5 for 3 days + normal RFT - Type-1 RTA.
Urine specific gravity < 1.005; urine osmolality < 200 mOsm/kg - Diabetes insipidus (up dilute urine).
Isosthenuria (urinary parameters = blood parameters) - ATN; CTID.

pages.traversal: 'High Colored Urine' heading; Presentation line; photo 'High coloured urine'; Causes: urological 90% (carcinoma bladder), nephrological 9%, hematological 1% (intravascular hemolysis); Approach: 1. Dipstick -> Positive -> Blood in urine / Negative -> porphyria, beetroot; 2. Centrifugation 1600 rpm 5 min; Clear supernatant -> RBCs settle -> glomerular criteria -> 3. Biopsy -> IgA mechanism; urological -> USG/CT; High coloured supernatant -> 4. undisturbed 3-6 h -> fades (myoglobin) / persists (hemoglobin).

elements.source: Presentation: hematuria - red, pink, tea or cola coloured urine.
Photo caption: High coloured urine.
Causes: Urological 90% (carcinoma bladder); Nephrological 9%; Hematological 1% (intravascular hemolysis).
1. Dipstick test -> Positive -> Blood in urine.
Negative -> Porphyria; up beetroot intake.
2. Centrifugation: 1600 rpm x 5 min.
Clear supernatant -> RBCs settle down.
Glomerular hematuria: >=40% dysmorphic RBCs / >=5% acanthocytes / single RBC cast with proteinuria.
3. Biopsy -> mesangial disease (IgA nephropathy): mesangial proliferation + matrix expansion -> capillary rupture.
Urological -> radiological investigation (USG abdomen, CT).
High coloured supernatant -> 4. sample undisturbed 3-6 h.
Colour fades -> myoglobin (short half-life); persists -> hemoglobin (long half-life).
Numbering 1-4 of the approach (page consolidation).

pages.traversal: 'Types of RBC' figure: Urological A crenated, isomorphic; Nephrological B dysmorphic, C acanthocytes (Mickey mouse RBCs); dipstick parameter table rows Leukocytes, Nitrites, Urobilinogen, Protein, pH, Blood, S.G, Ketones, Conj. bilirubin, Glucose; 'Factors affecting leucocyte urine dipstick test' seven bullets.

elements.source: Urological: crenated, isomorphic RBCs (A).
Nephrological: dysmorphic (B); acanthocytes - Mickey mouse RBCs (C).
Leukocytes / Nitrites - UTI (high specificity, poor sensitivity).
Urobilinogen - extravascular hemolysis.
Protein, pH, Blood, S.G, Ketones (SGLT2 inhibitors - euglycemic ketosis), Conj. bilirubin, Glucose (euglycemic glycosuria - proximal RTA).
Factors affecting leucocyte dipstick: seven bullets (cephalothin, tetracycline, cephalexin, tobramycin, glycosuria, proteinuria, concentrated urine).

pages.traversal: 'Proteinuria' heading; Urine protein / Uromodulin four bullets; Proteinuria levels table rows <150, 150-500, >500, >300 pregnancy; Albumin levels: injury chain; albumin table <30, 30-300, >300; moderately elevated albumin three bullets; Tests for proteinuria 1-4 with dipstick sub-bullets.

elements.source: Uromodulin/Tamm Horsfall: 70-80 mg/day; most abundant component of normal urine; forms matrix of casts.
Produced by thick ascending limb of loop of Henle.
<150 normal; 150-500 functional proteinuria (stress, anxiety, menses, protein supplements).
>500 significant proteinuria; >300 significant proteinuria in pregnancy.
Albumin -> tubular injury -> inflammation -> TGF-beta -> fibrosis.
Urinary albumin <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria; >300 albuminuria.
Moderately elevated albumin: marker of vascular integrity; up thrombosis risk (CVA, CAD) d/t endothelial injury; requires further evaluation.
Tests: 1. 24 hour urine protein; 2. spot PCR; 3. spot ACR.
4. Urine dipstick: qualitative; positive only ~800 mg; detects only albumin; supplement with PCR/ACR/24 h protein.

pages.traversal: 'Microscopic Examination'; cell size line; photos: phase contrast monomorphic RBCs with 'Large white cell' arrow, tubular epithelial cell with nucleus, oval fat bodies (Maltese cross inset), granular cytoplasm & lobulated nucleus; Polarizing microscope list (blood: babesiosis; kidney: Fabry's, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, prerenal azotemia); CASTS IN URINE formation DCT; table hyaline / coarse granular / fine granular.

elements.source: Cell size: RBC < WBC < epithelial cell.
Photo: 'Large white cell' arrow; caption 'Phase contrast microscopy with monomorphic red cells'.
Captions: 'Tubular epithelial cell with nucleus'; 'Granular cytoplasm & lobulated nucleus'.
Oval fat bodies -> Polarizing microscope: maltese cross appearance; in blood: babesiosis.
In kidney: Fabry's disease, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis, prerenal azotemia.
CASTS IN URINE - Formation: distal convoluted tubule (DCT).
Hyaline cast - normal; kidney disease.
Coarse granular cast (label only); fine granular cast - kidney disease.

pages.traversal: Cast table continued row by row: pigment fine granular, RBC, WBC, tubular epithelial (muddy brown), broad/waxy, fatty, eosinophil, fractured (on biopsy).

elements.source: Pigment fine granular cast - pigment nephropathy: hemolysis; rhabdomyolysis.
RBC cast - glomerular hematuria.
WBC cast - acute pyelonephritis; post streptococcal GN; ATN/Acute Interstitial Necrosis (AIN) as printed.
Tubular epithelial cast (muddy brown) - ATN/AIN (most specific).
Broad cast, waxy cast - chronic kidney disease.
Fatty cast - lipiduria (nephrotic syndrome); Fabry's.
Eosinophil cast - ATN/AIN.
Fractured cast (on biopsy) - myeloma.

pages.traversal: 'CRYSTALS IN URINE' figure panels A-G with captions: A uric acid rhomboid; B calcium oxalate dihydrate bipyramidal/envelope; C calcium oxalate monohydrate dumb bell; D calcium phosphate (alkaline urine) star; E struvite (MgNH4PO4) coffin lid; F cholesterol crystal; amoxicillin broom brush; G hexagonal cystine.

elements.source: A: Uric acid crystals - rhomboid.
B: Calcium oxalate dihydrate - bipyramidal/envelope shaped; C: monohydrate - dumb bell shaped.
D: Calcium phosphate (in alkaline urine) - star shaped.
E: Struvite (MgNH4PO4) - coffin lid appearance.
F: Cholesterol crystal (no shape descriptor).
Amoxicillin crystal - broom brush appearance.
G: Hexagonal cystine crystal (page consolidation after it).
